why: Cross-language test vectors for THE durable failure identity algorithm -- the CONTRACT spelling a persisted failure envelope carries, which is a different string from the runtime spelling in nominal-error-identity.json and is minted by a different function. Both backends mint it independently -- the reference frontend in poc/src/durable/site-id.ts (durableFailureIdentity) and the Go fork in compiler/forkbridge/durable.go.txt (durableFailureIdentity) -- and a persisted failure is only interoperable if the two agree byte for byte. Two hand-maintained copies of one algorithm is exactly the shape that produced the defect this file exists for, so the copies are pinned against each other HERE rather than against two separately maintained expectations that can drift apart unnoticed. Regenerate by RUNNING a backend, never by hand or from a report: poc/src/durable/durable-failure-identity.test.ts checks the reference against these rows, and compiler/fork_durable_identity_test.go compiles each viaFork row with the pinned fork and reads the identity back out of the emitted Plan.
algorithm: identity := "vibelang:" + escape(file) + "@" + escape(className) + "@1", where escape emits a UTF-16 code unit verbatim when it is in [A-Za-z0-9._/:-] and otherwise emits "+" followed by exactly four upper-case hex digits of the unit. '+' is withheld from the alphabet as the escape introducer, and '@' is withheld as the SEPARATOR, so the identity holds exactly two '@' and the parse is unambiguous. When the spelling exceeds 256 UTF-16 code units the identity is instead "vibelang.digest:" + lower-case hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the spelling + "@1". Nothing is folded and nothing is truncated, so two distinct (file, className) pairs never converge.
viaFork: false marks a row the Go fork cannot be handed as a FILE NAME at all: virtualFileName (compiler/forkbridge/main.go.txt) fail-closes on an absolute name, a name containing a colon, and an empty name, and the bridge protocol refuses a `vibe` file whose name does not end in `.vibe`. The two separator-destruction rows whose file name has no extension (`a.vibe_B`, `a.vibe#B`) are unreachable for that last reason -- they are reachable on the reference because compileActionContract takes any fileName, and they are the pair that proves escaping alone was not the fix, so they are pinned there rather than dropped. Those rows still pin the algorithm on the reference side; they are unreachable input for the end-to-end fork check, not exemptions from agreement.
